title: The Replication Database: Documenting the Replicability of Psychological Science
venue: Journal of Open Psychology Data 12:8, pp 1-23

selection.evidence: Reached from the Pawel-Held read as an out-of-sample test bed (2,164 pairs). Blinded copy: mark's 8 papers dropped before viewing.

cost.compute_notes: Data paper PDF from JOPD (23 pp; read pp 1-16, rest references/affiliations). Two data versions: frozen 2023-10-16 (osf qtkzy, CSV served under .xlsx name, 1,239 rows) and GitHub forrtproject/fred-data output/FReD.xlsx (commit 6743efb, 2026-02-01, 2,164 rows). Blinding filter f00; counts f05; forecasts f01-f04 (each < 2 min).

triggers: database of replication attempts psychology original replication pairs
what share of psychology replications succeed
replication effect size relative to original median
does replication sample size predict success
test replication forecasts or bias corrections on real data

claims.statement: The 16 Oct 2023 snapshot holds 1,239 original-replication entries (336 independent originals, 468 independent replication findings); outcomes: 641 informative failure, 447 success, 133 not available, 15 inconclusive, 3 practical failure. Replication effects are smaller than originals: relative effect size (k = 1,050) M = 0.52, SD = 0.98, Md = 0.387.
claims.scope: Liberal inclusion (any study naming the original it replicates); entries from Many Labs are per lab (ML1 352, ML3 145 of 1,239); effect sizes converted to r where possible.

quantities.name: fred2023_success_share
quantities.baseline: failure 641, NA 133, inconclusive 15, practical failure 3 -- all reproduce exactly

quantities.name: fred2023_relative_replication_es_median
quantities.baseline: M .524, SD .977, min -6.9, max 22.82 reproduce exactly

our_assessment.why: Every printed count reproduces from the frozen file except two bookkeeping numbers: unique ref_original 335 (printed 336 originals; may be a formatting duplicate) and rows lacking ES 188 (printed 201 not in quantitative analyses). Entries are not independent: 72.8% of usable pairs in the 2026 snapshot come from originals with more than one replication row (max 35), so per-entry rates over-weight Many Labs effects.

claims.statement: The database's 'power' column (replication power computed at the ORIGINAL effect size) has median 0.982 and is >= .8 for 59% of entries, while the success rate is 447/1,239. Read as a planning quantity it is almost uninformative about outcomes: the original effect it assumes is, by the database's own median, 2.6 times the replication effect.
claims.scope: Frozen 2023 version; power as computed by the database.

our_assessment.why: Direct computation from the file. The paper describes the variable correctly; the point is about what a reader should not do with it.

claims.statement: In the 2026 snapshot (2,157 rows after blinding, 1,082 usable pairs), the original's evidence predicts replication only weakly -- success rises from 26.6% to 50.7% across quintiles of |t_o|, AUC .625 -- and the replication's sample size (absolute or relative to the original) not at all: AUC .472, logit coefficient -0.054 (SE .075), while the standard replication-probability model implies a clear positive gradient (AUC .66).
claims.scope: Outcome = replication p <= .05 and not coded 'failed'; |t_o| from exact p or parsed 1-df statistic; cluster SEs by original.

our_assessment.why: Robust across the subsets in f02. The outcome coding is mine and not the database's (the database's 'success' also counts both-non-significant pairs); with the database's own verdict as outcome the forecast AUC drops below .5 (.476), which needs explaining before anyone uses that verdict as ground truth for a detector.

datasheet.composition: one row per original-replication effect pair; 70 columns incl. es_original/es_replication (r), n, refs, result, closeness_* codings, significant_*, power.
datasheet.caveats: Served as text/csv under an .xlsx name: pandas.read_excel fails. Rows are not independent (Many Labs per-lab rows).

artifacts.locator: https://github.com/forrtproject/fred-data output/FReD.xlsx (commit 6743efb, 2026-02-01; 2,164 rows x 56 cols, renamed columns: doi_o, n_o, pval_value_o, reported_success ...)

checked.how: python .../reanalysis/f00_blind_filter.py FReD.xlsx FReD_blinded.csv; then f01-f04 on the blinded copy
checked.result: 2,157 rows after the over-inclusive blinding filter; 1,082 usable for forecasting (exact or parsed original p, both n, usable replication p).

datasheet.composition: live database export; effect sizes as reported (es_value_o mixes numbers and test-statistic strings).
datasheet.caveats: Living resource: the 2026 export is not the 2023 analysed version; cite the commit. es_value_o is often a string like 'F(1, 188) = ...'.

relations.why: FReD used as the out-of-sample test bed for the Pawel-Held forecasts (that record's c7).

open_questions: Do the closeness_* variables (coded for a subset) predict success where |t_o| and n_r do not?

Why is the replication-probability forecast anti-correlated (AUC .476) with the database's own 'successful' verdict? Candidate: verdict criteria differ by source (Many Labs vs individual submissions).
Blinding: f00 drops rows for mark's 8 papers; remove after unblinding and rerun f01-f04.
